questions.question: The railway system connecting St-Petersburg to Vladivostok is ______.
questions.questionHtml: The railway system connecting St-Petersburg to Vladivostok is ______.
questions.solution: The correct answer is Trans-Siberian Railways. It is a major rail route of Russia that runs from St. Petersburg to Vladivostok, passing through Moscow, Ufa, Novosibirsk, Irkutsk, Chita and Khabarovsk. It is the longest double-tracked and electrified transcontinental railway in the world, and has helped open up Asia to West European markets. It runs across the Ural Mountains, Ob and Yenisei rivers, and has important agro and fur centres.

questions.question: In what form is the energy derived from the food that we eat is stored in our body?
questions.questionHtml: In what form is the energy derived from the food that we eat is stored in our body?
questions.solution: The energy derived from the food we eat is stored in our body in the form of glycogen. Glycogen is a complex carbohydrate that is stored in the liver and muscles. It is formed by the process of glycogenesis, where excess glucose is converted into glycogen. When the body requires energy, glycogen is broken down into glucose through the process of glycogenolysis.

The correct answer is 'Barren'.

Key Points

  • The most appropriate antonym of the given word 'Fertile' is 'Barren'
  • Fertile: (used about land or soil) that plants grow well in. [(ज़मीन या मिट्टी) उपजाऊ]

  • Barren: (used about land or soil) not good enough for plants to grow on. [(भूमि या मिट्टी) पौधों वृद्धि के लिए अनुपयुक्त, ऊसर, बंजर]
    • Example: He also wants to use the water to irrigate barren desert land.
       

Correct Answer: Barren.

Additional Information

  • Let's look at the meaning of other words:
    • Fecund: able to produce a lot of children, crops, young animals, etc. [(बच्चे, फ़सल आदि) ऊर्वर, बहुफलदायक, उपजाऊ, बहु प्रसव]

questions.question: Choose the option that can substitute the underlined segment correctly and complete the meaning of the sentence. Navika is a superb and impressive child in her class.
questions.questionHtml:
Choose the option that can substitute the underlined segment correctly and complete the meaning of the sentence.

Navika is a superb and impressive child in her class.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Brilliant'.

Key Points

  • The most appropriate word for the underlined part is 'Brilliant'.
  • Brilliant: extremely intelligent or skilled. (अत्यंत बुद्धिमान या कुशल)
    • Example: She seemed to have a brilliant career ahead of her
  • The correct collocation here is brilliant. We say 'a brilliant student' rather than 'a splendid/dazzling/vivid student'.
  • Thus, the correct answer is Option 2.
     

Correct Answer: Navika is a brilliant child in her class. 

Additional Information

  • Let's look at the meaning of other words:
    • Splendid: very good; excellent. (बहुत अच्‍छा; अत्‍युत्तम)
    • Dazzling: extremely bright, especially so as to blind the eyes temporarily. (चौंधिया देने वाला)
    • Vivid: having or producing a strong, clear picture in your mind. [सजीव और सुस्‍पष्‍ट (प्रभाव होने व उत्‍पन्‍न करने वाला)]

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Conceit
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Conceit
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Modesty'.

Key Points

  • The most appropriate antonym of the given word 'Conceit' is 'Modesty'.
  • Conceit: too much pride in yourself and your abilities and importance. (अहंकार, घमंड)
    • Example: He may be so conceited to believe that he is competent when he is not.
  • Modesty: the quality of not talking about or not trying to make people notice your abilities and achievements. (लोगों को आपकी क्षमताओं और उपलब्धियों के बारे में बात न करने या न करने की कोशिश करने का गुण)
    • Example: She does a lot of work for charities, but her modesty forbids her from talking about it.
       

Correct Answer: Modesty.

Additional Information

  • Let's look at the meaning of other words:
    • Concealment: the action of hiding something or preventing it from being known. (किसी चीज को छिपाने या ज्ञात होने से रोकने की क्रिया)
    • Reveal: to make something known that was secret or unknown before. [(गुप्‍त या पूर्वतः अज्ञात वस्‍तु को) प्रकट करना, रहस्‍य खोल लेना]
    • Hidden: to put or keep somebody/something in a place where he/she/it cannot be seen; to cover something so that it cannot be seen. (व्‍यक्ति या वस्‍तु को ऐसी जगह रखना जहाँ कोई देख न सके, छिपाना; किसी वस्‍तु को ऐसे ढकना कि वह दिखाई न दे, छिपा देना)

    • sample: a small number or amount of somebody/something that is looked at, tested, examined, etc. to find out what the rest is like. [नमूना (व्‍यक्तियों की थोड़ी संख्‍या या वस्‍तुओं की थोड़ी मात्रा जिसकी जाँच के आधार पर शेष व्‍यक्ति या वस्‍तु के विषय में पता चले कि वे कैसे या कैसी हैं)]

Key Points

  • The most appropriate title of the given passage is 'The Historical Work of Tacitus'.
  • In the fifth blank, the most appropriate word is 'probes'.
  • It means 'to ask questions in order to find out secret or hidden information'. (रहस्‍य या गुप्‍त बातें मालूम करने के लिए सवाल पूछना)
    • Example: The newspapers are now probing into the President’s past.

    • listens: to pay attention to somebody/something in order to hear him/her/it. (किसी बात को सुनने के लिए उस पर ध्यान देना)
    • imbibes: to absorb something, especially information. (ग्रहण करना या आत्मसात करना, विशेषकर सूचना; अन्तःशोषण करना)
  • Thus, the correct answer is Option 3.
     

Correct Passage: If writers only dared to dare, a Suetonius or a Tacitus of the Novel could exist, for the Novel is essentially the history of manners, turned into a story and a play, as is History itself often enough. And there is no other difference than this: that the one, the Novel, cloaks its manners under the disguise of invented characters, while the other, History, provides names and addresses. Only, the Novel probes much deeper than History.
